text:
maria: ran a focused bring-up for aries-13b (int8 vs int6) on chat-sim and longform slices, + quick unit-econ calc. TL;DR: int6 saves ~35% cost with a small avg quality drop that matters only on a few signal slices.
raj: nice — can you paste the numbers?
maria: sure, raw from the run (median across 3 seeds):
jen: :eyes:
maria: ```
int8 (aries-13b-int8)  - p50 latency: 48ms  p95: 230ms  tokens/s: 2100  human-win-rate: 87%  hallucination rate: 3.1%  cost per 1M toks: $180
int6 (aries-13b-int6)  - p50 latency: 40ms  p95: 180ms  tokens/s: 3000  human-win-rate: 84%  hallucination rate: 4.2%  cost per 1M toks: $118
Notes: measured on standard chat-sim (mix of short Q&A, followups, and >=1k token longforms).
```
steve: so int6 is ~34% cheaper and slightly faster. Quality gap is ~3pp on the average win-rate, hallucinations +1.1pp.
raj: where does the gap concentrate? doc edits / code tasks / summarization?
maria: mostly long-form creative summaries and nuanced step-by-step instructions. For short transactional chat (<=3 turns) win-rate delta is <1pp. For 1k+ token completions delta grows to ~6-8pp and hallucination delta ~+3pp.
jen: got it. any latency/regression surprises?
maria: p95 improved on int6, so latency SLOs look fine; kv-cache memory slightly better on int6 so more efficient at longer contexts.
infra-bot: deploy canary started for aries-13b-int6 on dedicated-pool-3 — 10% traffic -> 3 nodes.
raj: recommended routing to product/GTN? my instinct: default int6, fallback to int8 for longform or high-confidence prompts. agree?
maria: yes. propose: default route=aries-13b-int6, route-to-int8 when estimated quality risk > 0.05 (slice-based) OR request.tokens > 800 OR user flag:high_fidelity.
steve: can you sketch a routing policy payload we can hand to GTN?
maria: pasted below. small JSON for routing rule (prod):
{
  "primary_model":"aries-13b-int6",
  "fallback_model":"aries-13b-int8",
  "policy":{
    "conditions":[
      {"type":"tokens_greater_than","value":800},
      {"type":"slice_tag","value":"high-fidelity"},
      {"type":"explicit_user_flag","value":"quality_mode"}
    ],
    "action":"route_to_fallback_if_any_condition_true"
  },
  "canary":{"pct":10, "duration_hours":168}
}

jen: looks reasonable. we should add a telemetry hook: spike in contradictions and hallucination when fallback triggers.
maria: added monitoring TODO — surface avg logprob delta, hallucination rate, and human-win-rate sampled daily for the routed subset.
raj: unit-econ ask for GTN: show per-API-call delta. For a 3-turn chat avg length 200 toks, what's the per-call cost diff?
maria: quick calc: 200 toks * (1M toks price / 1,000,000) -> per-call cost. Using our numbers: int8: $180/1M -> $0.00018 per token -> per-call ~$0.036. int6: $118/1M -> $0.000118 per token -> per-call ~$0.024. Delta ~$0.012 per call (33% savings).
steve: meaningful at scale. if a product has 1M monthly chats, that's ~$12k/mo.
jen: any downside for low-tier users? lower latency + lower cost are wins, but product might prefer higher fidelity for discovery flows. Need opt-in.
raj: recommendation summary we can pass to GTN/product: 1) Default to aries-13b-int6 for general chat, 2) Route to aries-13b-int8 for: longform (>800 tokens), safety/verification tasks, and explicit quality_mode flag, 3) Start with 10% canary traffic to int6 (if going from int8 default) or to int8 (if deploying int6 as fallback) — whichever path product prefers, 4) Add daily quality telemetry and a rollback trigger if win-rate drop >3pp or hallucination +2pp on routed traffic.
maria: I'll draft a 1-paragraph blurb + minimal config snippet for GTN. cc @jen to review wording.
jen: happy to review. suggest adding a short UX caveat about perceived answer consistency when switching models mid-conversation.
maria: good point — recommend sticky-session by model for a conversation unless explicit re-eval. added to notes.
steve: can we also test a mid-tier quant (int7-ish / mixed-precision) later? might give most of the cost win with smaller quality hit.
maria: plan to run int7 mixed next week on a smaller slice, will share microbench.
raj: thanks — this is actionable. tagging product for GTN handoff. :thumbsup:
